blocks.0: In the Same Charter with the Jews
blocks.1: Many clauses of the charter are about the Jews.
blocks.3: And truly the Jews of Banu ‘Awf are one nation with the believers; for the Jews their din, for the Muslims their din; and so for their allies and for themselves.{{1}}
blocks.4: Part of one nation, but keeping religion separate. No condition of forcibly changing din is here. This same thing was written in separate clauses for the Jews of Banu al-Najjar, Banu al-Harith, Banu Sa‘idah, Banu Jusham, Banu Aws, Banu Tha‘labah.{{1}}
blocks.5: The share of expenses was stated separately too.
blocks.7: And truly the expenses of the Jews are on the Jews, the expenses of the Muslims on the Muslims. And whoever fights against the parties of this document, there will be mutual help among them against that one. And among them will be well-wishing and good counsel, and righteousness; not sin.{{1}}
blocks.8: And in the defence of the city?
blocks.10: And truly whatever event or dispute occurs among the parties of this document, of which corruption is feared, its decision returns to Allah and the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad. And Allah is witness to the most God-fearing and most righteous part of this document. And truly Quraysh and those who help them will not be given refuge. And whoever attacks Yathrib, there will be mutual help among them against that one.{{1}}
blocks.11: The city now belonged to all. If an outsider attacked, Jew and Muslim would stand together. Historians call this one of the first written constitutions of the world. Here no one’s religion was taken away; only the rules for living in one city were written.
blocks.13: At the end of the forty-seven clauses, a general declaration.
blocks.15: No earner earns except against himself. And truly Allah is witness to the truest and most righteous part of this document. And truly this writing will not be a barrier for an oppressor or a sinner. And truly whoever goes out is safe, and whoever stays in Madinah is safe; except one who has wronged and sinned. And truly Allah is the neighbour-protector of the one who does good and keeps taqwa. And Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.{{1}}
blocks.16: A state ends with these words; security for everyone, only not for the oppressor. Nowhere in this document is it written that anyone must change religion. What is written is only who is whose neighbour, who will take responsibility for whom, to whom to go in a quarrel. That a city can hold many kinds of people, this one writing is its proof.
blocks.17: The Charter of Madinah: Full Text
blocks.18: Many clauses of the charter have come until now in pieces. Now the whole text, in the charter’s own words, in the order of the clauses. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This written document is from Muhammad the unlettered Prophet, between the believers and Muslims of Quraysh and Yathrib, and those who follow them, join them and strive with them. 1. Truly they are one nation, distinct from other people. 2. The Muhajirun of Quraysh will remain on their former custom; they will bear blood-money among themselves, and ransom their captives by the custom and fairness current among the believers. 3. And Banu ‘Awf will remain on their former custom; they will bear blood-money by the old rule, and every party will ransom its captives by the custom and fairness current among the believers. 4. And Banu al-Harith will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 5. And Banu Sa‘idah will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 6. And Banu Jusham will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 7. And Banu al-Najjar will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 8. And Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 9. And Banu al-Nabit will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 10. And Banu Aws will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 11. And the believers shall not abandon among themselves one bent under debt or distressed by the burden of many dependants; in the matter of ransom or blood-money, they shall give to him according to custom. 12. And no believer shall make a pact with the freed ally of another believer, excluding him (his master). 13. And the God-fearing believers will be against the one among them who transgresses or seeks any scheme of injustice, sin, enmity or corruption among the believers; all their hands will be on him, even if he is the child of one of them. 14. And no believer shall kill a believer for the sake of a disbeliever, nor help a disbeliever against a believer. 15. And truly the protection of Allah is one; the lowest of them can give refuge. And the believers are friends of one another, to the exclusion of other people. 16. And whoever of the Jews follows us shall have help and equal treatment; he will not be wronged, nor will anyone be helped against him. 17. And the peace of the believers is one; in war in the way of Allah no believer shall make peace without the other believers, except on terms of equality and fairness. 18. And every party that goes out on an expedition with us shall relieve one another in turn. 19. And in the blood shed in the way of Allah, the believers are equal sharers with one another; and the God-fearing believers are on the best and straightest path. 20. And no polytheist shall give refuge to the property or life of Quraysh, nor stand as a barrier on his behalf against any believer. 21. And whoever kills a believer wrongfully, with proof, shall be subject to retaliation, unless the guardian of the slain is satisfied. All the believers are against him; nothing is lawful for them except standing against him. 22. And truly it is not lawful for a believer who has affirmed what is in this document and believes in Allah and the Day of Resurrection to help or shelter one who commits a new crime. Whoever helps or shelters him, upon him is the curse and wrath of Allah on the Day of Resurrection; from him no obligatory or voluntary act will be accepted. 23. And in whatever matter you differ, its decision returns to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to Muhammad {{1}}. 24. And the Jews will bear the expense with the believers, as long as they are at war. 25. And the Jews of Banu ‘Awf are one nation with the believers; for the Jews their din, for the Muslims their din; and so for their allies and for themselves. But whoever wrongs and sins will destroy only himself and his family. 26. And for the Jews of Banu al-Najjar, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf. 27. And for the Jews of Banu al-Harith, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf. 28. And for the Jews of Banu Sa‘idah, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf. 29. And for the Jews of Banu Jusham, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf. 30. And for the Jews of Banu Aws, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf. 31. And for the Jews of Banu Tha‘labah, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf; but whoever wrongs and sins will destroy only himself and his family. 32. And Jafnah, a branch of Tha‘labah, are like themselves. 33. And for Banu Shutaybah, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf; and righteousness, not sin. 34. And the allies of Tha‘labah are like themselves. 35. And the close associates of the Jews are like themselves. 36. And none of them will go out (to war) without the permission of Muhammad. There will be no barrier on the path of retaliation for a wound. Whoever attacks suddenly will bring it upon himself and his family, unless he is wronged. Allah is witness to the most righteous part of this matter. 37. And the expenses of the Jews are on the Jews, the expenses of the Muslims on the Muslims. Whoever fights against the parties of this document, there will be mutual help among them against him. Among them will be well-wishing and good counsel, and righteousness; not sin. No one will be sinful because of his ally. And help is for the wronged. 38. And the Jews will bear the expense with the believers, as long as they are at war. 39. And the interior of Yathrib is sacred, forbidden ground, for the parties of this document. 40. And the neighbour is like oneself; he is not to be harmed, nor is he sinful. 41. And no honoured protected person shall be given refuge without the permission of his guardians. 42. And whatever event or dispute occurs among the parties of this document, of which corruption is feared, its decision returns to Allah and the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad {{2}}. Allah is witness to the most God-fearing and most righteous part of this document. 43. And Quraysh and those who help them will not be given refuge. 44. And whoever attacks Yathrib, there will be mutual help among them against him. 45. And if they are called to peace, they will make peace and accept it. If the believers too are called likewise, it will bind the believers too, except one who fights against the din. Each group’s share is for its own side. 46. And the Jews of Aws, their allies and themselves, will be in the same rights as the parties of this document, with good treatment from the parties of this document; and righteousness, not sin. 47. No earner earns except against himself. Allah is witness to the truest and most righteous part of this document. This writing will not be a barrier for an oppressor or a sinner. Whoever goes out is safe, and whoever stays in Madinah is safe; except one who has wronged and sinned. Allah is the neighbour-protector of the one who does good and keeps taqwa. And Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah {{3}}.{{4}}
blocks.20: ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) asked for the road to the market. That market too the Prophet {{1}} himself had fixed. In one narration he looked at the market of the Nabit (the Nabataean people), and said, this is not your market. He looked at another market, that too did not please. Coming back from a third place he said,
blocks.22: This is your market. Here no place will be assigned, and no tax will be imposed on it.{{1}}
blocks.23: The chain is weak, so this cannot be taken as evidence. Only as a scene; that Madinah had an open, tax-free market, this much is supported by other narrations and history too. On the road to that market ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) walked. Not anyone’s mercy; the earning of his own hands.
blocks.25: The charter makes brothers on paper. But the Prophet {{1}} wanted the bond to descend into the heart too. So he kept saying the same thing in different ways.
blocks.26: The believers, in mutual mercy, love and compassion, are like one body; when any limb of the body hurts, the whole body stays awake, shivering with fever.{{1}}
blocks.27: When one hurts, the whole body is awake. Through the pain of one, the whole society is meant to be stirred. Another time he interlaced his fingers one with another and showed.
blocks.28: A believer is to another believer like a wall; each holds the other firmly. Saying this, he interlaced his fingers together and showed.{{1}}
blocks.29: A brick does not stand alone. The brick beside it holds it up. And the smallest, hardest measure he said in one sentence.
blocks.30: None of you will be a believer until he likes for his brother what he likes for himself.{{1}}
blocks.31: What I want for myself, the same for my brother. With this one measure one can check oneself every day.
blocks.33: This forming of the state at Madinah returns to our home today at several places. The first place is the manner of helping. Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA) wished to give half his wealth. ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) did not take it; he took only the road to the market. Sa‘d did not insist either; he showed the road and stopped. Today when we go to help someone we often make them small. In the manner of alms, reminding again and again of the favour. When a person is made small in taking help, the fault is the giver’s. There is a dignified manner of giving; learning it is important.
blocks.34: The second place is that of one body. When calamity comes in a neighbour’s house, do we shiver with fever, or just ask for news and finish? The third place is that of the written document. The Prophet {{1}} did not stop at an oral promise; he had it written, so that no one could later deny. The understandings in our families and institutions that remain oral, how many take the form of writing?
blocks.35: The fourth place is that of one nation within difference. In the Charter of Madinah, Muslims and Jews in the same city, under the same charter, yet to each their own religion. Today around us too there are people of other views; neighbours, colleagues, relatives. The city is everyone’s, the rule is meant to be just for everyone.
blocks.36: The fifth place is that of the right to correct. Salman (RA) stopped Abu al-Darda’ (RA), and the Prophet {{1}} endorsed it. Today, seeing the excess of a friend or brother, do we have the courage to stop them, or do we stay silent and save the relationship?
blocks.37: The sixth place is the neighbour’s. ‘The neighbour is like oneself’; this one line of the Charter of Madinah. Today do we know the name of the person in the next flat, the next house? The seventh place is the night guest. Putting out the lamp, that Ansari couple passed the night without eating. The guest did not even understand. Today when we feed someone we announce it on social media. The one whose name did not even remain in history, his sacrifice is the deepest.
blocks.38: The eighth place is the date-orchard proposal. The Ansar had wanted to give away the land; the Prophet {{1}} did not agree and chose the exchange for labour. Today, helping someone, we often think donating is the greatest gift. Yet a task, a partnership, an opportunity; these too are help of equal worth, and keep someone’s self-respect intact even more.
blocks.39: The ninth place is not spreading word without verifying. Even in the single question of whose brother the Prophet {{1}} himself was, Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Kathir remained careful; where there is no chain, they said plainly there is no chain. Today we spread what we hear about beloved people and beloved leaders without verifying. Spreading a wrong piece of information even in the name of love is wrong; however great the person concerned may be.
blocks.40: The tenth place is gratitude. The Muhajirun, having received so much, were still afraid: has all the reward gone to them? The Prophet {{1}} showed the way, du‘a and praise. Today we take a favour from someone and either forget it or consider it a burden. When did we last pray from the heart for someone?
blocks.42: In today’s dars we saw how a city became a state. One call; the adhan, first uttered through the voice of a slave of not long before. One bond; the brotherhood of Muhajirun and Ansar, where instead of half the wealth someone asked only for a road. One writing; the Charter of Madinah, where Muslims and Jews in the same city, under the same law, yet each in their own religion.
blocks.43: The manner of Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA) is the lesson of this dars. He wished to give half his wealth, but when ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) asked only for the road, he did not insist. The giving hand must always be kept wide, but no one has the right to make the taking hand small. That breadth of Sa‘d, Allah Himself sealed in Surah al-Hashr; putting others first even in one’s own want. In the next dars we will see how the qiblah changed in this new state, and how the rulings came step by step.
blocks.44: So take one deed with you from today’s dars.
blocks.46: The Ansari brother wished to give half the wealth; the Muhajir brother took only the road to the market, and between the two there was no being made small. Today I will ask myself a question: when I help someone, does their self-respect get a scratch?
blocks.47: Today I will help someone by showing just a way, not by donating; which I will not leave from today on.

footnotes.0: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Hisham, Dustur al-Madinah, clause 25
footnotes.1: Separate clauses for the Jewish tribes: Dustur al-Madinah, clauses 26–35.
footnotes.2: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Hisham, Dustur al-Madinah, clause 37
footnotes.3: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Hisham, Dustur al-Madinah, clauses 39, 44
footnotes.4: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Hisham, Dustur al-Madinah, clause 47
footnotes.5: Full text of the Charter of Madinah: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Ibn Hisham, ‘His {{1}} document between the Muhajirun and the Ansar and the treaty with the Jews’ (Islamweb edition, vol. 1, pp. 501–504) and Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (‘Dustur al-Madinah’, clauses 1–47). A translation compiled from the two texts; a document of the Sirah, not a hadith. In Ibn Hisham’s text it begins with ‘Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim’, in Ibn Kathir’s citation it does not. In clause 11 Ibn Hisham explains ‘mufrah’ as ‘bent under debt and distressed by the burden of many dependants’. Clauses 24 and 38 are identical in Ibn Hisham (‘yunfiqun’, will bear the expense); in Ibn Kathir’s clause 24 there is ‘yattafiqun’; Ibn Hisham’s text has been given preference. There are variant readings in ‘dasi‘ah’ (Ibn Hisham) and ‘dasisah’ (Ibn Kathir) in clause 13, ‘al-birr al-mahd/al-muhsin’ (two forms in Ibn Hisham) in clause 46, and ‘yabi’u ba‘duhum ‘ala ba‘d’ and ‘yabi’u ba‘duhum ba‘da’ in clause 19; in the translation the most common meaning has been taken.
footnotes.6: Sunan Ibn Majah 2233 (from Abu Usayd (RA)); al-Busiri: the narrators of the chain are weak

quiz.q: What does the charter say about the Jews of Banu ‘Awf?
o: They are one nation with the believers; for the Jews their religion, for the Muslims their religion
They must leave Madinah, which is in no clause of the charter, which is in no clause of the charter at all
They must accept Islam, which is contrary to the charter’s main aim
They will have no rights, which is contrary to the charter’s last clause

quiz.q: According to the charter, what will the Jews and Muslims do in the defence of Madinah?
o: Each defend their own area separately, which is contrary to the charter’s idea of joint defence
Help one another if the partners of the charter are attacked
Only the Muslims will take the responsibility of defence, which is contrary to the charter’s clause of being one nation
When an external enemy comes the Jews will leave the city

quiz.q: What does the principle of ‘one nation, different religions’ in the charter with the Jews show?
o: The Jews too must pray
The Jews will be subject citizens under the Muslims
The Jews have no right to property
Partners in civil rights
quiz.e: In clauses 25–35 the same thing is repeated.

quiz.q: In an institution, workers of different faiths work together. Which principle of the Charter of Madinah can be applied?
o: Asking everyone to follow the same religion, which is a method contrary to the main aim of the charter
The same rules for all, but no interference in anyone’s religion
Giving the people of different faiths separate rules, which is a method contrary to the main aim of the charter
Excluding the people of different faiths
quiz.e: Clause 25: for the Jews their religion, for the Muslims their religion.

quiz.q: If people of another religion in an area are attacked, what should Muslim neighbours do, in the light of the charter?
o: Look only to their own security, although the charter speaks of joint defence
Stand beside them as partners of the charter
Stay away from the event, although the charter speaks of joint defence
Just pray and sit
quiz.e: Clauses 39, 44: the pledge of mutual defence.

quiz.q: In the last clause of the Charter of Madinah, whom was security not given?
o: Those who leave Madinah
Those who do business
Those who oppress or commit sin
Those who keep relations with another tribe

quiz.q: What is the meaning of ‘the one who goes out is safe, the one who stays is safe’ in the last clause?
o: Security is for everyone except the oppressor and the criminal
Leaving the city means no protection, although there is no such opposite statement in the clause
Only those who go to war are safe, although there is no such opposite statement in the clause
Security is only for the rich

quiz.q: What did ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) first bring back from the market?
o: A date stone of gold
A goat
A bolt of cloth
Ghee and cheese

quiz.q: In one weak narration, what did the Prophet ﷺ say about the market of Madinah?
o: Here no place will be assigned
In this market only Muslims will trade
In this market the prices of all goods will be fixed
This market will be closed on Friday
quiz.e: Sunan Ibn Majah 2233; al-Busiri: the narrators in the chain are weak.

quiz.q: What do ‘Abd al-Rahman’s (RA) asking for the road to the market and the tax-free market of the weak narration show together?
o: Madinah’s market was only for the Muhajirun, although they could go to the market
In Madinah there was an opportunity of one’s own earning instead of anyone’s mercy
Going to the market was forbidden, although trading was not forbidden
Trading was makruh
quiz.e: A tax-free open market gave people like ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) an opportunity.

quiz.q: What comparison did the Prophet ﷺ give of the believers to one another?
o: Like a river whose flow does not stop, which is the simile of a different hadith
Like one body; in the pain of one the whole body stays awake
Like a desert where everyone is alone, which is a simile that came in no hadith
Like a market where everyone is a competitor

quiz.q: What comparison did the Prophet ﷺ give by interlacing his fingers?
o: A believer is to another believer like a shade
A believer is to another believer like a mirror
A believer is to another believer like a wall
A believer is to another believer like a lamp

quiz.q: What is the rest of the hadith ‘None of you will be a believer until...’?
o: He prays five times a day, which is about a different hadith
He gives food to the neighbour, which is about a different hadith
He reads the Qur’an daily, which is about a different hadith, although it is not part of this hadith here
He likes for his brother what he likes for himself

quiz.q: The hadith of one body and the hadith of the wall of interlaced fingers; what do the two teach together?
o: Believers must always stay together
Believers must have the same profession
The bond of believers is not only in words
Believers’ wealth must be equal

quiz.q: When a person becomes small in taking help, whose fault is it; what is the dars’s main lesson?
o: The one who takes help should feel ashamed
Help should not be taken at all, although the dars encourages taking help
In the manner of giving; not insisting, just showing the way
A helper should always expect repayment, although the dars says not to desire repayment
quiz.e: The manner of Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA) teaches this lesson.
